> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/http-conformance/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be3cc7280b9625af914b7b4a978396368f0ee92` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8429de97e523cb814b2acccd137e5a440588d1fb` — the merge of head `6544c545a43182b45f413816cfb937676753f940` into base `7be3cc7280b9625af914b7b4a978396368f0ee92`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8429de97e523cb814b2acccd137e5a440588d1fb && git checkout 8429de97e523cb814b2acccd137e5a440588d1fb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7be3cc7280b9625af914b7b4a978396368f0ee92 6544c545a43182b45f413816cfb937676753f940 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7be3cc7280b9625af914b7b4a978396368f0ee92 && git merge --no-ff 6544c545a43182b45f413816cfb937676753f940

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be3cc7280b9625af914b7b4a978396368f0ee92
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7be3cc7280b9625af914b7b4a978396368f0ee92` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:cli` seat 1 · `os-sales` · session `session_01BVm1pAXVXQ3PjC42j1kPFf` · 2026-10-18T02:03Z

Head `6544c545a`. This is the seat's review of record for #24083 (claim `6243784478`, amended by the seat's ruling `6244250024`; dev reports `6244221751` (round 0) and `6244500210` (patch round 1)). No contract face is touched:
- `Clause-②: no`. `@objectstack/http-conformance` is `"private": true`, and no published accept set or contract moves;
- no `packages/spec/**` or `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/**` path;
- the PR is not governed.

So CI plus the seat's own read decide it.

- **Form:**
  - Draft → `main`. The body's first line is `Fixes #24083`, its only closing keyword (scanned). `Clause-②: no` is line-initial.
  - `skip-changeset`, for a private package whose README change ships nothing.
  - The seat applied the dev's ten round-1 body replacements at this head (each matched once, read back byte-identical) and retitled the notes section "Acceptance notes".
- **The ruling executed as ruled (MATCH, not imported):**
  - `adapter.ts` decides the body the way `plugin-hono-server`'s `readRequestBody` does, with module-private copies:
    - declared JSON: empty is `{}`, anything else that does not parse is refused;
    - forms (`multipart/form-data`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) are parsed by Node's own `Response.formData()` into the standard transport's field shape;
    - any other media type that carries a body by its framing headers is refused on read, and one with no body is `{}`.
  - The four refusal messages are verbatim. `rawBody()` still returns the bytes of a refused body. Nothing is imported from the subject, and no dependency or export is added.
- **The seat's own read of the code (`adapter.ts` at this head):**
  - `req.body` is an accessor: a read of a refused body records it and throws it. A route that reads only `rawBody()` never meets it, and the setter stays.
  - `refusalStands()` drops every write after a refused read, on a route and in the fallback. `writeBodyRefusal` then answers `400 {success:false,error:{code:'INVALID_REQUEST',message}}`, the two keys the standard transport renders.
  - On a route this happens on both the return path and the catch path. In the fallback it runs before the `500 Fallback handler failed` and before the unmatched 404/405, which is `runHandler`'s order on the standard transport (`plugin-hono-server` `adapter.ts:1302-1304`, `:880`).
  - Unchanged: the generic catch arm (`statusCode` → `{error}`), and the fallback's `500` for a throw that read no refused body (`fallback-seam` G5-a). `setFallbackHandler`'s guarantees 2 and 4 still hold as written, and guarantee 4 now names its one exception.
- **Proof:**
  - Over a real socket, 17 route shapes and 12 fallback shapes answer the same status and body bytes on both adapters. The one exception is the pre-existing `; charset=utf-8` on the reference's JSON `Content-Type`.
  - `request-body.conformance.test.ts` pins this per adapter, with a 16-row byte-parity block (40 tests).
  - Two ablations, each once and with the restore proven:
    - round 0 put back the old `catch { body = {}; }` arm: 2 red, every `hono` leg green;
    - round 1 deleted the fallback's refusal-answer line: 6 red (the three node fallback legs and their parity rows), every `hono` leg and both controls green.
  - The suite is 190/190 and typecheck holds its ledger unchanged.
  - The `test:repo` projects for core, objectql, rest, runtime, types and spec (re-run in round 1) all exit 0.
  - eslint exits 0, and the 52-command union is 51 exit 0 with 1 NOT-MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which needs every package's `dist/`; CI's Lint & Repo Gates ran it green).
- **Prose faces, sentence by sentence against the diff:**
  - The PR body's table rows, the answer-side bullet, the coverage list and the parity paragraph match the code above. ✓
  - The README line now reads "JSON and forms (multipart included) are parsed into `req.body`, and every other media type stays raw behind the lazy `req.rawBody()`", which is what `readRequestBody` does. ✓
  - The adapter's docblocks (`refusalStands`, `writeBodyRefusal`, guarantee 4) state what their code does. ✓
- **Acceptance notes, routed, each `carrier: none`:**
  - The `setFallbackHandler` sentence in `packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts` names no refused-read exception. That wording is the spec lane's, held off here, and shows no wrong answer.
  - The write-then-read shape that `node:http` cannot replace is documented in `writeBodyRefusal`.
  - Middleware receives the real request; the middleware contract does not populate `body`.
  - The pre-existing `charset` difference.
- **The dev's process note** (`skip-changeset` written by a separate `label-write` stroke, where `os-dev.md` on `main` says `pr_create`'s labels) goes to the seat's round report. The label is on the PR.
- **CI on this head:** 47 check runs, 37 success and 10 skipped, none red, read in this act. The skips are the opt-in and full-battery lanes, `Check Changeset` on the `skip-changeset` fast path, and the body-edit re-runs of `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`; each of those two also has a success row. The three body guards re-ran on the edited body and passed.
- **Landing:** not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 24242`: 0 of 3 paths on the register; 606 changed lines ≤ 3000). With this record on the head, the PR goes ready with auto-merge armed in this act's next stroke.
